newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault expects loss for 1996 - Le Monde.
newsitem.headline: Renault expects loss for 1996 - Le Monde.

text.p: Renault SA chairman Louis Schweitzer said in a newspaper interview on Wednesday that he expected the carmaker to show a loss for the full year.

Asked by the afternoon daily Le Monde whether he expected a full-year loss, Schweitzer was quoted as saying, "It's our primary assumption given the state of our market forecasts." "The truck operations are not improving. The car division will fare better. But not sufficiently, as the two positive factors -- a pursuit of our cost reductions and a renewed model line-up -- will not compensate for the price war," he said.

Renault on Tuesday reported its net attributable profit shrank in the first half of 1996 to 158 million francs ($30.6 million) from 1.76 billion in the first half of 1995, as its car operation lost 911 million francs and its trucks operating income plummeted.
Renault said the car operation would show only a slight improvement in the second half from the prior year's 1.35 billion franc operating loss.
It said in its earnings statement that the trucks division would show an operating loss in the second half of 1996.
